title: fix(lint): field-no-consumers credits row-level security predicates and the inline grid's line-position field
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBD51tXwx3Q3tVXsAku498wA)_

Closes #32256

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`field-no-consumers` 不再把两类其实有人读的字段报成「没人用」：① 权限集行级安全策略 `rowLevelSecurity[].using` / `.check`（以及对象自己的 `defaultRowScope`）里按字段过滤或校验的字段；② 内联明细表拖拽排序时写入、加载时按它排序的「行序字段」（如 `position`）。spec 新增一个纯函数 `deriveInlineGridSortField`，按渲染器同一规则算出这个字段，名单本身仍不公开。showcase 白名单里为这两个误报加的两条随之删除。
- 为什么改：showcase 上 `showcase_invoice.owner`（被 `invoice_own_rows` 的 `using` 每次查询读取）和 `showcase_invoice_line.position`（发票明细表的行序字段）被误报；PR #32233 只能先把它们列进白名单。
- 风险与回滚：只是一条建议级（warning）lint 少报误报，不拒收任何元数据；spec 只多一个导出函数，不改任何 schema。权限集里除行级策略以外的路径（字段级授权等）仍算「只携带不读取」。回滚即 revert。
- 先看：① `packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts` 的 `isRlsPredicateSite` 与 `creditInlineGridSortField`（两处计入点）；② `packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-columns.ts` 的 `deriveInlineGridSortField`；③ `examples/app-showcase/test/author-time-advisories.test.ts` 删掉的两条白名单。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-field-consumers.test.ts -t 32256`，预期两组共 16 条全绿（行级策略 9 条、行序字段 7 条）。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **`packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.ts`, credit 1: a row-level security predicate is a read.** `CARRIER_ROOTS` still lists `permissions`, and every path under it stays a carrier except a policy's two predicate clauses, `permissions[].rowLevelSecurity[].using` and `.check`. Those are now `behaviour` sites, and their text is scanned as an expression (every bare identifier a candidate), because a policy names its fields as bare CEL identifiers (`owner == current_user.email`). The policy's `object` is the context the walk already resolves, so the field is credited on the object the policy filters, never on another object declaring the same name.
  - `using` is compiled into the row filter of every read, update and delete the policy governs (ADR-0056 D4); `check` is matched against every row an insert or update writes (ADR-0058 D4). Both read the field on every request, as a sharing-rule `condition` (already credited) does.
  - The key names are typed against the spec rather than read from it: `'rowLevelSecurity' satisfies keyof PermissionSet`, and `['using', 'check'] satisfies readonly (keyof RowLevelSecurityPolicy & keyof DefaultRowScope)[]`. The spec exports no list of a policy's predicate clauses (its own refinement names the same two members by hand), and `satisfies` turns a rename there into a typecheck failure here instead of a credit that quietly stops matching.
  - **Same class, fixed in place:** an object's `defaultRowScope` (`DefaultRowScopeSchema`, enforced by `plugin-security`'s `object-default-row-scope.ts`) is the same policy with the object implied. It was already a behaviour site under `objects`, but `using` / `check` were not scanned as expressions, so a field only it filters on was reported `inert` (repro in Acceptance notes). The same predicate test now covers `objects[].defaultRowScope.using` / `.check`, keyed by `'defaultRowScope' satisfies keyof ServiceObject`.
- **Credit 2: an inline grid's line-position field is a read.** The renderer resolves, on every inline grid, the child field it stamps each line's position into on drag-reorder and orders the child rows by (`deriveDetail` in `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/deriveMasterDetail.ts`; `MasterDetailForm.tsx` sets `sortField` from it on both the authored-columns and the derived branch and adds it to the child fetch's `$orderby`). No column draws it: both spec derivations skip the sort-position names. The rule now credits that field as `behaviour` through the spec's own derivation on each carrier that draws a grid: a `lookup` / `master_detail` field that sets `inlineEdit` (authored `inlineColumns` or derived), and every `subforms` / `details` collection entry. A `record:line_items` panel is not credited: it does not go through `deriveDetail`.
- **`packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-columns.ts`: new `deriveInlineGridSortField(def)`** on `@objectstack/spec/data`. The renderer's rule, reproduced exactly: the first child field, in field-map order, whose name is one of `INLINE_GRID_SORT_FIELDS`; no flag or type is consulted; `undefined` when the child declares none or carries no field map. `INLINE_GRID_SORT_FIELDS` stays private (no barrel re-export, no subpath), as its module says. The module note gains a section on it. Generated `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain the one line.
- **`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`.** `os explain field-no-consumers` lists both reads among the consumers, and the carrier paragraph says "a field-level permission grant".
- **`examples/app-showcase/test/author-time-advisories.test.ts`.** The two `field-no-consumers` allow-list entries #32233 added for these false positives (`showcase_invoice.owner`, `showcase_invoice_line.position`) are deleted, with their section heading. The list is two-directional, so it now requires both findings to be gone.
- **`.changeset/32256-field-consumers-rls-and-grid-position.md`.** `patch` for `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec`, with both declaration lines.

Responsibility: `CARRIER_ROOTS` with `permissions`, and the branch where a carrier root decides the bucket before anything else is asked, came in with the rule itself (`a87163c89b`, #16323). The later inline-grid credits (#20929, #20951, #21091) covered the columns, the join key and the row form, never the line-position field; the renderer derives that field from the child since objectui#11070, after the authored `sortField` was retired.

## Why

#32256: the QA run for #32168 found both showcase findings (class a) and #32233 allow-listed them as a workaround. The card asks for both credits, a negative for each, and the two entries off once #32233 merged. It merged as `d391babc`; this branch is on it. Seat ruling on the card (claim amendment 2): route A, one spec helper; `INLINE_GRID_SORT_FIELDS` stays private.

Prior rulings read (`check-prior-rulings.mjs --card 32256 --terms field-no-consumers,CARRIER_ROOTS,rls,inline-grid`, 35 hits): ADR-0056 D4 and ADR-0058 D4 decide that `using` and `check` are compiled and enforced, which is why both clauses count as reads; ADR-0058 D5 (security predicates fail closed) changes nothing here. The other hits (ADR-0054 §3, ADR-0055 §1/§4, ADR-0056 D2/D3/D9, ADR-0058 D1/D6) touch RLS enforcement, not this rule.

## Tests

All new lint pins are top-level `describe` blocks in the rule's existing harness, `packages/lint/src/validate-field-consumers.test.ts`, placed above the two `#22161` blocks that must stay last (they read what the cases above fired).

**`[#32256] … a row-level security predicate reads the fields it names`** (9 cases). Two objects (`inv`, `other`) both declare `owner`; `inv` also declares `region`.

- Baseline: no policy, `owner` reported on both.
- `using` (`owner == current_user.email`) credits `inv.owner`; `check` on an `update` policy credits it the same way.
- A compound `using` credits every field it names (`owner`, `region`).
- A name-keyed `permissions` map reads the same as the array shape.
- An object's `defaultRowScope` with `using` and `check` credits `inv.region` and `inv.owner`.
- ⛔ A field-level grant beside the policy stays a carrier: `inv.region` is `carrier-only` with exactly `permissions[0].objects.inv.fields.region`.
- ⛔ The predicate credits only the object it filters: `other.owner` stays `inert`.
- ⛔ The same predicate text under an ordinary object key (`description`) credits nothing.

**`[#32256] … an inline grid reads its line-position field`** (7 cases). The child `lin` declares `position` then `sort_order`.

- Baseline: a `lookup` with no `inlineEdit` leaves both sort-named fields reported.
- A grid with authored `inlineColumns: [{ name: 'qty' }]`, and one with derived columns, both credit `position` only.
- A form view `subforms` entry and an `object-master-detail-form` `details` entry credit it on their `childObject`.
- The field is the first sort name in the child's FIELD order: with `sort_order` declared first, `sort_order` is credited and `position` reported.
- ⛔ The child's second sort-named field stays reported, and so does a sort-named field on the parent.

**`packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-columns.test.ts`, `deriveInlineGridSortField`** (5 cases): resolves the declared name; first match in field order, not list order; flags and type are not consulted; the resolved name is one both derivations leave out; a look-alike name (`order`, `rank`) and a missing field map resolve `undefined`.

## Acceptance notes

- **`current_user.*` paths.** In an RLS predicate, `current_user.email` matches the rule's `.x` reference shape, so a field named `email` on the policy's object would also be credited. That is the scan every expression site already gets (a sharing-rule `condition` included) and the quiet direction the rule's header chooses ("under-crediting is the noisy direction"). Not narrowed here.
- **A field permission's `when`** (`permissions[].objects.X.fields.Y.when`, a CEL row condition on the edit vote) is still a carrier, as the card asks ("every other path under `permissions` stays a carrier"). It does read the fields it names; whether that is a consumer is not decided here. carrier: none.
- **`defaultRowScope` repro (in-place fix).** Before this branch, `validateFieldConsumers({ objects: [{ name: 'o', defaultRowScope: { operation: 'select', using: "region == 'emea'" }, fields: { name: { type: 'text' }, region: { type: 'text' } } }], views: [{ list: { data: { object: 'o' }, columns: [] } }] })` returned `region` as `inert` (measured on the built lint dist, `[["region","inert"]]`). The four in-place conditions hold: same defect class, the same predicate test, a file this claim holds, the same gate family. The showcase declares no `defaultRowScope`, so the showcase readings do not move.
- `packages/spec/src/data/inline-grid-sort-fields.ts` still says "Two readers here"; the new helper sits in one of them (`inline-grid-columns.ts`), so the sentence stays true and the file is untouched.
